chief_complaint: Recent acute ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) with ongoing management and newly diagnosed metastatic prostate cancer
history_of_present_illness: The patient suffered an acute STEMI on 2024-03-09 and has been placed on dual antiplatelet therapy, a beta‑blocker, high‑intensity statin, and antihypertensive therapy. In July 2024 metastatic prostate cancer was diagnosed, with concurrent carcinoma in situ and a primary prostate neoplasm. Hypertension remains uncontrolled (BP 142/102) despite a hydrochlorothiazide/losartan combination. The patient continues daily tobacco use (since 1997) and uses a nicotine patch, indicating a partial cessation attempt. He has obesity (BMI >30), pre‑diabetes (A1c 5.9%), anemia, major depressive disorder, osteoarthritis of the knee, chronic sinusitis, and significant psychosocial stressors including social isolation, limited transportation, and a criminal record. Wellness visits dominate his encounter history, with only one emergency and one inpatient encounter recorded.
